Bengal Partition

§ 2Content

§ 3BENGAL PARTITION: 1905

  • Lord Curzon (1899-1905), the then Viceroy of India, proposed the partition in 1905.
  • The partition created a divide between Hindus and Muslims, leading to communal tensions that would echo throughout India's struggle for independence.
  • Bengal constituted 1/4th of the total British India population.

§ 4Revolutionary Policies of Lord Curzon

  1. 1. Calcutta Corporation Act, 1899
  2. 2. Official Secrets Act, 1904 (to curb the freedom of Press)
  3. 3. Indian University Act, 1904
  4. 4. Bengal Partition, 1905

§ 5Bengal was divided into:

  1. 1. East Bengal (Muslim) → At present: Assam and Bangladesh
  2. 2. West Bengal (Hindu) → At present: West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar

§ 6Reasons given by Britishers for Partition of Bengal

  • The British justified the partition of Bengal in 1905 primarily on grounds of administrative convenience and the need to improve governance in a region with a large and diverse population.
  • The actual reason was to "Weaken the Bengal" (the nerve centre of Nationalist activities).
  • Partition announced on: July, 1905
  • Partition came into force on: October, 1905

§ 7SESSIONS OF CONGRESS

§ 81905 Session of Congress

  • The Session happened in Benaras and was presided over by G. K. Gokhale.
  • It approved Anti Partition Movement / Swadeshi Movement.
  • The formal proclamation of the Swadeshi Movement (foreign made goods and products were to be boycotted) was made on 7th August 1905 in Calcutta Townhall.

§ 91906 Calcutta Session of Congress

  • It was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.
  • Four Important Resolutions were Taken in this Session:
  • Swaraj as a goal adopted
  • Boycott of foreign goods
  • Swadeshi
  • National Education (formation of National Education Council)

§ 101907 Surat Session of Congress

  • It was presided by Rash Behari Ghosh.
  • In this Session, the Congress split into Moderates and Extremists.

§ 11Reasons for their Separation

  • The role of the INC in the manner of opposing the Partition of Bengal was the main cause of the Split.
  • The Extremists wanted the agitation to be a mass struggle all over the country. But the Moderates still had faith in the British administration over the wanted to confine the boycott to Bengal and foreign goods only.
  • Britishers adopted "Carrot and Stick Model" within Congress.
  • Carrot: Appeasement to Moderates; Stick: Suppressing Extremists.

§ 12MODERATES AND EXTREMISTS

§ 13Methods adopted by Moderates were: Petitions, newspapers, pamphlets

Moderates

  • SN Banerjee, KK Mitra, GK Gokhale, Pherozshah Mehta, etc.

Extremists

  • Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Aurobindo Ghosh

Note: Bande Matram journal was written by Bipin Chandra Pal.

§ 14Methods Adopted by Extremists

According to Extremists:

  • They had hatred for foreign rule; since no hope could be derived from it.
  • Swaraj to be goal of national movement.
  • Direct political action was required.
  • Belief in capacity of masses to challenge the authority.
  • Personal sacrifices required and a true nationalist to be always ready for it.
  • Formation of Swadesh Bandhab Samiti by Ashwini Kumar Dutta at Barisal (in Bangladesh now).
  • National Educational Centres to be formed.
  • Indigenous Enterprise: Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company by V.O. Chidambaram Pillai in Tamil Nadu

§ 15Bal Gangadhar Tilak

  • He organised Ganpati, Shivaji festivals to attract and mobilise the youth (in Maharashtra).
  • He was titled as "Father of Indian Unrest" By Valentine Chirol in his book "India Unrest".
  • He is famously known as "Lokmanya Tilak".
  • Newspapers Published:
  • Mahratta (in English)
  • Kesari (in Marathi)

§ 16Newspapers during Anti-partition Movements

  • Hitabadi by: Dwijendranath Tagore
  • Sanjibani by: Krishna Kumar Mitra
  • Bengalee by: Surendranath Banerjee
  • B.G. Tilak said that: Freedom is my Birth Right and I Shall have it.

§ 17Revolutionary Activities (continued)

  • 1899: Mitra Mela was founded by Savarkar Brothers in Poona
  • 1901: Mitra Mela was merged with Abhinav Bharat Society by V D Savarkar
  • 1905: Indian Home Rule and Indian House was formed by Shyamji Krishna Verma in London
  • Journal written: The Indian Sociologist
  • 1907: Madam Bhikaiji Cama became the first Indian to hoist Indian Flag on foreign soil (in Stuttgart, Germany). She published journal Vande Mataram.
  • The flag hoisted by Madam Bhikaiji was smuggled into British India by Indulal Yagnik
  • 1908: Alipore Bomb Conspiracy / Manicktolla Bomb Conspiracy (this was an attempt to murder judge of Muzaffarpur) → Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki were involved in this. Kanailal Dutta killed the witness of this incident.
  • Prafulla Chaki committed suicide and Khudiram Bose was hanged in Muzaffarpur jail.
  • 1909: Madan Lal Dhingra killed Curzon Wyllie
  • 1909: AMT Jackson was killed by Anant Lakshman
  • 1910: United India House (in USA) was founded by Taraknath Das and G.D. Kumar
  • 1913: Ghadar Party was formed in San Francisco (HQ: USA) by:
  • Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna (First President of Gadar), Barkatullah, Parmanand, Kartar Singh
  • 1915: Berlin Committee was formed by Virendranath Chattopadhyay

In 1911, V. D. Savarkar was sent to Cellular jail in Andaman & Nicobar Islands

§ 18Komagata Maru Incident, 1914

  • A Japanese ship taken on lease by Sikh businessman and sailed to Vancouver (Canada) from Hong Kong.
  • This incident involved a ship carrying 376 Indian passengers, primarily Sikhs who were denied entry to Canada due to discriminatory immigration laws. Forced to return to India, they faced further mistreatment, highlighting the struggle against racial discrimination and colonial operation.

§ 19Defence of India Act 1915

  • This Act was enacted by the British government in India to suppress the Ghadrites particularly in Punjab, during World War I.
  • This Act was later replaced by a Permanent Act called Rowlatt Act.

§ 20World War I

  • In 1914, World War I began → It was fought between the Central Powers and the Allied Powers.

Allies of World War I (they won the war)

  • Belgium, France, Great Britain (and Commonwealth), Italy, Japan, Russia, and USA

The Central Power

  • Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria, Germany, and Ottoman Empire (Turkey)

§ 21Abanindranath Tagore

  • He painted the image of Bharat Mata in 1905. The painting was a symbol of nationalism during the Indian independence movement.
  • He was the principal artist of Indian School of Oriental Art (1907) and founder of the Bengal School of Art.

§ 22Actions to Show Unity

  • People tied Rakhi to each other to show unity
  • Rabindranath Tagore wrote a song: Amar Sonar Bangla (now it is National Anthem of Bangladesh).
  • Sadrasa Geethangal, a collection of poems was written by Subramaniya Bharti.
  • People sang Vande Matram (National Song); however Government banned it.

The painting of Bharat Mata

§ 23Leaders

  • Poona and Bombay: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
  • Delhi: Sayed Haider Raza
  • Madras: Chidambaram Pillai
  • Punjab: Lala Lajpat Rai

§ 24Response of Muslims

  • Muslims did not support Anti-Partition Movement.
  • Formation of All-India Muslim League on 30th Dec 1906 in Dhaka (now Bangladesh) by Nawab Khwaja Salimullah and Aga Khan.

§ 25INDIA COUNCIL ACT, 1909

  • The Indian Council Act of 1909 is also known as Morley-Minto Reform.
  • Lord Morley was the then Secretary of State and Lord Minto was the then Viceroy of India.
  • The provision for separate electorate for Muslim was introduced by Lord Minto (he is also known as "Father of Communal Electorate")
  • Viceroy Executive Council will have one Indian → First Indian to be a part of it was Satyendra Prasad Sinha.

§ 26Annulment of Partition

  • In 1911, Lord Hardinge II organised Delhi Durbar (3rd Delhi Durbar) for the coronation of King George V (capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911) → Delhi Durbars have been organised three times in: 1877, 1903, 1911.
  • In 1911, King George V announced the reunification of Bengal during the Delhi Durbar.

§ 27REVOLUTIONARY ACTIVITIES

  • 1902: Anushilan Samiti (Bengal) was formed by Satish Chandra Basu, Jatindranath Banerjee, Barindra Kumar Ghosh
  • In Patna, this Samiti was founded by Sachin Sanyal
  • 1890: Shivaji and Ganpati festivals organised
  • 1897: The Chapekar brothers assassinated W. C. Rand (Plague Commissioner of Poona)

§ 28During the World War I, in the context of the Indian nationalist:

  • The Moderates supported the war as a matter of duty.
  • The Extremists supported the war, hoping for future self-governance in return.
  • While the Revolutionaries, saw the war as an opportunity to actively fight against British rule and seek immediate Independence through forceful means.

§ 29HOME RULE LEAGUE (HRL), 1916

  • Two Home Rule Leagues were formed by: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant, both in 1916.
  • After B G Tilak's death in 1920, his Home Rule League was re-named as Swarajya Sabha by M K Gandhi.
Bal Gangadhar Tilak's HRLAnnie Besant's HRL
HQ: PoonaHQ: Madras
It was founded first.It had more branches of HRL.
Centre: Maharashtra (excluding Bombay City), Karnataka, Central Province, BerarCentre: Madras and Bombay City

§ 30LUCKNOW SESSION, 1916

  • This session was presided over by Ambika Charan Mazumdar.
  • In this session:
  1. 1. Reunion of Extremists and Moderates
  2. 2. Lucknow Pact (a Joint Pact) was signed between INC and Muslim League.

§ 31Writings

  • New India and Common Weal by: Annie Besant
  • Al Hilal (a weekly Urdu-language newspaper) by: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (he also wrote a book: India Wins Freedom)
  • Comrade (a weekly English-language newspaper): Maulana Md. Ali

§ 32Aurobindo Ghosh

  • He was born on 15 August 1872 in Calcutta.
  • He joined the revolutionary group Anushilan Samiti of Calcutta in 1902.
  • He edited the journal Vande Mataram and Yugantar.
  • He was associated with the Calcutta session of Congress in 1906.
  • In 1910, he withdrew himself from active politics.

§ 33Vande Mataram Movement

  • The song Vande Mataram was a part of Bankim Chandra Chatterji's novel Anand Math (1882).
  • It was the National Song of the Indian Independence movement.
  • It was set to tune by Rabindranath Tagore.

§ 34(Continued from previous pages)

§ 35Reaction of Muslims

  • Muslims did not support Anti-Partition Movement.
  • All India Muslim League was formed in December 30, 1906 at Dhaka (now in Bangladesh) by Nawab Khwaja Salimullah and Aga Khan.

§ 36Leaders:

  • Poona and Bombay: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
  • Delhi: Sayed Haider Raza
  • Madras: Chidambaram Pillai
  • Punjab: Lala Lajpat Rai

§ 37End of Bengal Partition

  • In 1911, King George V announced the reunification of Bengal during the Delhi Durbar.
